problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}=1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin

feedback.problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $\frac{{y}^{2}}{25}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
a=\sqrt{25}=5,\,b=\sqrt{9}=3.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are $y=\pm \frac{5}{3}x.$
